---
title: Create a Google Group
---

# Create a Google Group

This runbook creates a real Google group in your Google Workspace or Cloud Identity organization, as a Terragrunt unit in an infrastructure repository laid out like `infra-live`. Nothing here is simulated: the **Apply** tab creates the group, and the last step deletes it again.

## Before you start

- **Terragrunt 1.1.4 or later and OpenTofu 1.12.6 or later** on your `PATH`, the versions the repository's `root.hcl` requires.
- **AWS access to the account that keeps the repository's state.** Every unit keeps its state in S3, including units that manage another provider.
- **An admin who can create groups**, such as a Groups Admin or Super Admin, to sign in as.
- **A Google Cloud project** for this runbook. Google bills its API calls to that project, so you need permission to use its services, which an Owner or Editor has. Once you sign in, the block below checks which of its APIs to turn on.
- **A GitHub account** that can push to the repository below.
- **A Desktop app OAuth client** for Google Sign-In, from that project's **Google Auth Platform → Clients** page. Choose its JSON in the sign-in tab, or point `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_CREDENTIALS` at it before you start Runbooks.

## Sign in to Google

Sign in as the admin, and pick the project from above. The extra scopes let the form suggest your organization's domains and people.

<GoogleAuth
  id="google-auth"
  title="Sign in to Google"
  description="Sign in as an admin who can create groups, and pick the project for this runbook."
  defaultTab="oauth"
  scopes={[
    'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform',
    'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-identity.groups',
    'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.domain.readonly',
    'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user.readonly',
    'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email',
    'openid',
  ]}
/>

## Sign in to AWS

The repository's `root.hcl` keeps the unit's state in the production account's `us-west-2` bucket, so the plan and apply need AWS credentials for that account. Sign in with your organization's AWS access portal, then pick that account and a role that can read and write the state. A profile set up with `aws configure sso` fills in the portal's start URL and region.

<AwsAuth
  id="aws-auth"
  title="Sign in to AWS"
  description="Sign in to the AWS account that keeps the repository's state."
  defaultTab="sso"
  defaultRegion="us-west-2"
/>

## Clone the repository

The group's code goes in a pull request to this repository. It's a sandbox copy of the live infrastructure repository, laid out the same way.

<GitHubAuth
  id="github-auth"
  title="Sign in to GitHub"
  description="Sign in to GitHub to clone the repository and open the pull request."
/>

<GitClone
  id="clone-repo"
  githubAuthId="github-auth"
  title="Clone the repository"
  description="Clone the repository the group's code goes in."
  prefilledUrl="https://github.com/fabricahq/sandbox-infra-live"
/>

## Create the group

Fill in the group, and **Generate** writes it into the clone as `google/<domain>/groups/<email>/terragrunt.hcl`. The unit includes the repository's `root.hcl` for state and `config/google-provider.hcl` for the Google provider, as its GitHub and Cloudflare units do.

<TfModule
  id="group"
  source="google-group"
  template="templates/google-group-unit"
  path="google/{{ if .domain }}{{ .domain }}{{ else }}{{ .customer_id }}{{ end }}/groups/{{ .id }}"
/>

## Apply the group

Check the code on **Code**, open a pull request that adds it on **PR**, then plan and apply on **Apply**. The unit runs in the clone.

<TfApplyWithGitHubPullRequest
  id="apply-group"
  tfModuleId="group"
  title="Create the group"
  description="Opens a pull request with the group's unit, and applies it."
/>

<Admonition type="note" title="If the plan can't find your organization">
The module finds the organization's customer ID from its domain through Cloud Resource Manager, which works only when the domain has a Google Cloud organization. If it doesn't, clear **Organization**, and give the **Customer ID** under **Advanced options** instead. It's on the **Account settings** page of the Google Admin console.
</Admonition>

## Check the group

<Command
  id="show-group"
  title="Show the new group"
  description="Prints the group's outputs from the apply."
  env={{
    GROUP_EMAIL: "{{ .outputs.apply_group.email }}",
    GROUP_RESOURCE: "{{ .outputs.apply_group.resource_name }}",
    GROUP_CONSOLE: "{{ .outputs.apply_group.console_url }}",
  }}
  command={`echo "Group:         $GROUP_EMAIL"
echo "Resource name: $GROUP_RESOURCE"
echo "Admin console: $GROUP_CONSOLE"`}
/>

## Clean up

When you're done trying it out, delete the group with the same code and state. This can't be undone: the group's email archive goes with it.

<Command
  id="delete-group"
  title="Delete the group"
  description="Runs terragrunt destroy on the unit the apply ran, in the clone."
  env={{
    UNIT_DIR: "{{ .outputs.clone_repo.clone_path }}/{{ .outputs.group.CODE_PATH }}",
  }}
  command={`terragrunt --working-dir "$UNIT_DIR" --non-interactive destroy -auto-approve -input=false -no-color`}
  successMessage="The group is deleted."
/>
